q: Named National Artist for Architecture in 2014 and regarded as the master of Ecclesiastical Architecture, who defined the modern Catholic aesthetic in the mid-20th-century Philippines?
n: Jose Maria Zaragoza (2014), master of Ecclesiastical Architecture, defined the modern Catholic aesthetic in the Philippines, advancing the use of modern technology and materials in religious structures.

q: Alongside Peter Eisenman and Michael Graves, which architect belonged to the New York Five?
n: Richard Meier was a member of the New York Five, alongside Peter Eisenman, Michael Graves, Charles Gwathmey, and John Hejduk.

s: The Philippine Institute of Architects (PIA) Founders
q: Which architect helped found the Philippine Institute of Architects (PIA) together with Juan Nakpil, Tomas Mapua, and Carlos Barretto?
n: Tomas Arguelles was a founding member of the Philippine Institute of Architects (PIA), alongside Juan Nakpil, Tomas Mapua, Andres Luna de San Pedro, and Carlos Barretto.

q: Whose championing of indigenous materials — bamboo, rattan, coconut, capiz shells — in upscale contemporary design led to the Coconut Palace in Pasay City, and earned National Artist for Architecture recognition?
n: Francisco Mañosa championed indigenous materials — bamboo, rattan, coconut, and capiz shells — in contemporary design, and designed the Coconut Palace, Pasay City, 'Tahanang Pilipino,' showcasing the versatility of the coconut tree.

q: Which Deconstructivist architect represented the Office for Metropolitan Architecture (OMA)?
n: Rem Koolhaas represented the Office for Metropolitan Architecture (OMA) in the Deconstructivist Architecture exhibition.

q: Which architect, alongside Jose Maria Zaragoza and Carlos Arguelles, belonged to the Hexagon Architects collective?
n: Gavino De Leon was part of the Hexagon Architects collective, alongside Jose Maria Zaragoza, Carlos Arguelles, Edmundo Lucero, Francisco Fajardo, and Cezar Vergel de Dios.

q: Who designed the CCP Main Theater, the Philippine International Convention Center (PICC), and Brunei's Istana Nurul Iman as a National Artist for Architecture?
n: Leandro V. Locsin designed the CCP Main Theater, the Philippine International Convention Center (PICC), and the Istana Nurul Iman (Palace of the Sultan of Brunei) — his largest single work.

q: The Austrian firm led by Wolf Prix and Helmut Swiczinsky, featured in the Deconstructivist Architecture exhibition, is known by what name?
n: Coop Himmelb(l)au, the Austrian firm led by Wolf Prix and Helmut Swiczinsky, was featured in the Deconstructivist Architecture exhibition.

s: The Philippine Institute of Architects (PIA) Founders
q: In which year did the Philippine Institute of Architects (PIA) come into being?
n: The Philippine Institute of Architects (PIA) was founded in 1933.

q: Serving as Bauhaus Director alongside Walter Gropius and Ludwig Mies van der Rohe, who was this figure?
n: Hannes Meyer was a Director of the Bauhaus, alongside Walter Gropius and Ludwig Mies van der Rohe.

q: Graduating from Drexel Institute in 1908, who became the first of the pensionado architects?
n: Carlos Barretto was the first pensionado architect, graduating from Drexel Institute in 1908.

q: What title did the core members of the Metabolist Group give to their drafted manifesto?
o: Metabolism: The Proposals for a New Urbanism
n: The Metabolist Group's core members drafted the manifesto 'Metabolism: The Proposals for a New Urbanism.'

q: Officially formed for the 1960 World Design Conference in Tokyo, which younger generation of architects and critics is this?
n: The Metabolist Group was officially formed for the 1960 World Design Conference in Tokyo.

q: Known as the most prolific of the pensionado architects, who designed the Manila Central Post Office and the Metropolitan Theater?
n: Juan Arellano, the most prolific of the pensionado group, designed the Manila Central Post Office and the Metropolitan Theater.

q: Whose work reconstructing and expanding Quiapo Church, plus the UP Administration and Library buildings (Quezon Hall), earned him National Artist for Architecture honors?
n: Juan F. Nakpil's notable works include the reconstruction and expansion of Quiapo Church and the UP Administration and Library buildings (Quezon Hall), UP Diliman.

q: Which architect joined Kisho Kurokawa, Fumihiko Maki, Masato Otaka, and Noboru Kawazoe in drafting the Metabolist manifesto?
n: Kiyonori Kikutake was one of the five core members who drafted the Metabolist manifesto 'Metabolism: The Proposals for a New Urbanism.'

q: Who took the role of chief architect for the 1922 Manila Carnival?
n: Juan Arellano served as chief architect of the 1922 Manila Carnival.

q: Whose breakthrough 1933 project, the Ideal Theater in Manila, made his name in cinema design and later earned him National Artist for Architecture status?
n: Pablo S. Antonio's 1933 breakthrough project, the Ideal Theater in Manila, established his reputation in cinema design.

q: Which architect, a key Memphis Group collaborator, is also counted among the New York Five?
n: Michael Graves was a key collaborator of the Memphis Group and also a member of the New York Five.

q: Completing the Pioneer Triumvirate alongside Juan Nakpil and Tomas Mapua, name this architect.
n: Juan Arellano was part of the Pioneer Triumvirate, alongside Juan Nakpil and Tomas Mapua.

q: Recognized in 2006 as the 'Father of Philippine Landscape Architecture' for pioneering the field locally, who earned the National Artist for Architecture title that year?
n: Ildefonso P. Santos Jr. ('IP Santos'), National Artist for Architecture (2006), is regarded as the 'Father of Philippine Landscape Architecture,' emphasizing that nature and the built environment must coexist.

q: Which member of the New York Five eventually shifted toward Postmodernism?
n: Michael Graves, a member of the New York Five, later pivoted to Postmodernism.

s: The Philippine Institute of Architects (PIA) Founders
q: Established in 1933, what was the Philippines' first professional organization for architects?
n: The Philippine Institute of Architects (PIA), founded in 1933, was the first professional organization for architects in the Philippines, with founding members among the elite architects of the pre-war era.

q: Sto. Domingo Church in Quezon City — arguably his most famous work, a National Cultural Treasure blending Spanish Colonial 'Mission style' with Modernism — is credited to which National Artist for Architecture?
n: Jose Maria Zaragoza designed Sto. Domingo Church, Quezon City, arguably his most famous work and a declared National Cultural Treasure, fusing Spanish Colonial 'Mission style' with Modernism.

q: Curated by Philip Johnson and Mark Wigley for MoMA in 1988, the exhibition 'Deconstructivist Architecture' showcased which architectural movement?
n: The Deconstructivists were the architects featured in the seminal 1988 MoMA exhibition 'Deconstructivist Architecture,' curated by Philip Johnson and Mark Wigley.

q: Formed to design and build the National Library of the Philippines in Manila and named after its six prominent members, what was this collective called?
n: Hexagon Architects was formed to handle the design and execution of the National Library of the Philippines in Manila, named 'Hexagon' for its six prominent architects.

q: Nakpil received the National Artist for Architecture title in which year?
n: Juan F. Nakpil was named National Artist for Architecture in 1973, the first to receive the honor.

q: Known for exploring the 'intersections' of history and space, which Deconstructivist architect is this?
n: Daniel Libeskind focused on the 'intersections' of history and space.

q: The Bauhaus traces its founding to which year?
n: The Bauhaus was founded by Walter Gropius in 1919.

q: Founded by Walter Gropius in 1919 and steered by a 'Council of Masters' merging craft, art, and technology, which school is this?
n: The Bauhaus was founded by Walter Gropius in 1919 and led by a 'Council of Masters' who integrated craft, art, and technology.

q: Whose early, radical drawings stood out in the Deconstructivist Architecture exhibition?
n: Zaha Hadid was known for her early radical drawings in the Deconstructivist Architecture exhibition.

q: Published in 1972, what book featured the work of the New York Five?
o: Metabolism: The Proposals for a New Urbanism
n: The New York Five's work was featured in the 1972 book Five Architects.

q: Recognized for his furniture design contributions as a Bauhaus Master Teacher, who is this figure?
n: Marcel Breuer was a Bauhaus Master Teacher known for furniture design.

q: Designing the Manila City Hall and the Agriculture and Finance Building, who was the youngest among the pensionado architects?
n: Antonio Toledo was the youngest pensionado, and designed the Manila City Hall and the Agriculture and Finance Building.

q: Regarded as the 'Dean of Filipino Architects,' who received the first-ever National Artist for Architecture award in 1973?
n: Juan F. Nakpil was the first National Artist for Architecture (1973), regarded as the 'Dean of Filipino Architects,' a pioneer who believed in a distinctly 'Philippine Architecture.'

q: As professor and mentor to many of the Metabolist Group's core members, who gave them their platform at the 1960 World Design Conference?
n: Kenzo Tange was the professor and mentor to many Metabolist Group architects, using his prestige to give them a platform at the 1960 World Design Conference.

q: Responsible for the elaborate Neo-Classical and Art Deco pavilions of the Manila Carnival (1908-1939), which group of architects is this?
n: The Manila Carnival Architects designed the pavilions and structures for the Manila Carnival (1908–1939), a playground for testing Neo-Classical and Art Deco styles.

q: Recognized in 1976 as the pioneer of modern Philippine architecture for clean lines, plain surfaces, and attention to natural light and ventilation, who earned National Artist for Architecture status?
n: Pablo S. Antonio (1976) is considered the pioneer of modern Philippine architecture, prioritizing function over ornament and designing buildings for the comfort of their occupants.

q: Reacting against Modernism's 'good taste,' which Milan-based design and architecture collective did Ettore Sottsass found in 1980?
n: The Memphis Group was founded by Ettore Sottsass in 1980 as a Milan-based collective reacting against the 'good taste' of Modernism.

q: Rendering the 1935 Manila Carnival infrastructure in Art Deco style, who was the architect?
n: Carlos Barretto designed the 1935 Manila Carnival infrastructures in Art Deco style.

q: Nicknamed the 'Poet of Space' for concrete structures that seem to 'float,' and designer of the CCP complex, which National Artist for Architecture (1990) is this?
n: Leandro V. Locsin (1990), nicknamed the 'Poet of Space,' mastered the use of massive concrete made to look ethereal, appearing to 'float,' and designed the CCP Main Theater, a masterclass in Brutalist architecture.

q: Alongside Martine Bedin and Aldo Cibic, which figure co-founded the Memphis Group?
n: Michele De Lucchi was a core member/founder of the Memphis Group, alongside Martine Bedin, Aldo Cibic, Nathalie Du Pasquier, Matteo Thun, and George J. Sowden.

s: The Triumvirate of Modern Philippine Architecture
q: Completing the Triumvirate of Modern Philippine Architecture with Juan Nakpil and Leandro Locsin, name this architect.
n: Pablo Antonio, alongside Juan Nakpil and Leandro Locsin, forms the Triumvirate of Modern Philippine Architecture.

q: Known as 'IP Santos,' which National Artist for Architecture contributed landscape work at the San Miguel Building (Ortigas, Pasig City) and Luneta Park, Manila?
n: Ildefonso P. Santos Jr.'s notable landscape works include the San Miguel Building (Ortigas, Pasig City), Luneta Park (Manila), Tagaytay Highlands, and the renovation of Paco Park, Manila.

q: Which architect served as the bridge connecting the New York Five to Deconstructivism?
n: Peter Eisenman, a member of the New York Five, bridged the gap between that group and Deconstructivism.

s: The Philippine Institute of Architects (PIA) Founders
q: Which architect was among the founders of the Philippine Institute of Architects (PIA) in 1933?
n: Andres Luna de San Pedro was a founding member of the Philippine Institute of Architects (PIA) in 1933, alongside Juan Nakpil, Tomas Mapua, Tomas Arguelles, and Carlos Barretto.

q: Declared in 2018 and famous for the line 'I design Filipino, nothing else,' who was this leading advocate of Neo-vernacular architecture?
n: Francisco 'Bobby' Mañosa (2018) was the most vocal advocate for Neo-vernacular architecture, famously stating 'I design Filipino, nothing else,' and spent his career refining the Bahay Kubo and Bahay na Bato into modern structures.

q: Which architect's Santa Monica residence stood as a key example in the 1988 Deconstructivist Architecture exhibition?
n: Frank Gehry's Santa Monica house served as a primary example in the 1988 Deconstructivist Architecture exhibition.

q: Recognized as the master of Ecclesiastical Architecture, which member of the Hexagon Architects collective is this?
n: Jose Maria Zaragoza, master of Ecclesiastical Architecture, was part of the Hexagon Architects collective.

q: Locsin's National Artist for Architecture title dates to which year?
n: Leandro V. Locsin was named National Artist for Architecture in 1990.

q: Associated with the Parc de la Villette project, which Deconstructivist architect is this?
n: Bernard Tschumi is known for the Parc de la Villette project.

q: Ettore Sottsass established the Memphis Group in which year?
n: The Memphis Group was founded by Ettore Sottsass in 1980.

q: Who was responsible for founding the Bauhaus in 1919?
n: Walter Gropius founded the Bauhaus in 1919.

q: Sent to the U.S. as government scholars during the American colonial period to study Neo-Classical and Beaux-Arts design, which group of Filipino architects is this?
n: The Pensionados were the first Filipino architects sent to the U.S. as government scholars to study the Neo-Classical and Beaux-Arts style, later returning to lead the Bureau of Public Work.

q: Curated by Philip Johnson and Mark Wigley, what was the title of the landmark 1988 MoMA show that featured the Deconstructivists?
o: Metabolism: The Proposals for a New Urbanism
n: 'Deconstructivist Architecture' was the seminal 1988 MoMA exhibition, curated by Philip Johnson and Mark Wigley, that showcased the Deconstructivists.

q: Serving as a Bauhaus Master Teacher alongside Marcel Breuer and Wassily Kandinsky, who is this figure?
n: Paul Klee was a Bauhaus Master Teacher, alongside Marcel Breuer, Wassily Kandinsky, László Moholy-Nagy, and Josef Albers.

q: The first registered architect in the Philippines, and founder of the Mapua Institute of Technology, was which pensionado architect?
n: Tomas Mapua was the first registered architect in the Philippines and founder of Mapua Institute of Technology.

q: Advocating for a distinct 'Philippine Architecture' that merged local tradition with modern structural demands, which National Artist for Architecture is this?
n: Juan F. Nakpil espoused a style he called 'Philippine Architecture,' integrating local traditions with modern structural necessities, and was a major figure in establishing the Philippine Institute of Architects (PIA).

q: One of the five core drafters of 'Metabolism: The Proposals for a New Urbanism,' name this architect.
n: Fumihiko Maki was one of the five core members who drafted 'Metabolism: The Proposals for a New Urbanism.'

q: Credited with the 1917, 1920, and 1921 Manila Carnival designs, who was this architect?
n: Tomas Mapua designed the 1917, 1920, and 1921 Manila Carnivals.

q: Designer of the Far Eastern University (FEU) Campus in Manila — the city's largest collection of Art Deco buildings — which National Artist for Architecture is this?
n: Pablo S. Antonio designed the FEU Campus in Manila, considered the largest collection of Art Deco structures in Manila, featuring the Nicanor Reyes Hall, Engineering building, and Administration building.

q: Who established the Memphis Group in 1980?
n: Ettore Sottsass founded the Memphis Group in 1980.

q: Credited with laying the foundations of the architecture profession in the early-20th-century Philippines, what name is given to this trio?
o: The Triumvirate of Modern Philippine Architecture
n: The Pioneer Triumvirate refers to Juan Nakpil, Tomas Mapua, and Juan Arellano, credited with establishing the foundations of the profession in the Philippines.

q: Designer of the Church of the Holy Sacrifice at UP Diliman — the country's first circular Catholic church with a thin-shell concrete dome — which National Artist for Architecture is this?
n: Leandro V. Locsin designed the Church of the Holy Sacrifice, UP Diliman, the first Catholic church in the country with a circular design and a thin-shell concrete dome.

q: Also known as 'The Whites' and featured in the 1972 book Five Architects, which group of five New York City architects is this?
n: The New York Five, also known as 'The Whites,' were featured in the 1972 book Five Architects, sharing an obsession with the pure, white, geometric forms of early Le Corbusier.

s: The Triumvirate of Modern Philippine Architecture
q: Rounding out the Triumvirate of Modern Philippine Architecture alongside Juan Nakpil and Pablo Antonio, who is this architect?
n: Leandro Locsin, alongside Juan Nakpil and Pablo Antonio, forms the Triumvirate of Modern Philippine Architecture.
